mechanism_narrative: The sharp drop in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT, paired with higher RESIDENTIAL, implies more time spent near home and fewer discretionary trips. That pattern should continue to suppress retail visits over the next four weeks as reduced commuter flow lowers incidental shopping traffic.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not below the last 28 days despite WORKPLACES staying depressed and RESIDENTIAL staying elevated.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT falls more than 10 points week-on-week, retail access weakens quickly because fewer people pass through commercial areas during commutes. This should lower RETAIL_REC within one week and remain visible for up to two weeks unless transit rebounds.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline in the week after a transit drop of more than 10 points, or rises despite sustained transit weakness.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous slide in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT indicates a tightening mobility regime that removes both employment-linked and in-route retail demand. The combined shock should push RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks more than either series alone.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to fall over the next 28 days when both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain below their recent averages.

mechanism_narrative: Rising GROCERY_PHARM alongside falling RETAIL_REC signals substitution toward essential, lower-discretion trips. If that split persists, retail-and-recreation mobility should remain weaker over the next two weeks as households consolidate nonessential outings.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises while RETAIL_REC falls for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stops declining or rebounds within two weeks despite continued gains in GROCERY_PHARM.

mechanism_narrative: A broad decline in PARKS, TRANSIT, and WORKPLACES marks generalized mobility contraction rather than a category-specific shift. Under that constellation, retail-and-recreation trips should fall further over the next four weeks as all trip-generating channels weaken together.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not lower over the next 28 days even though PARKS, TRANSIT, and WORKPLACES remain depressed.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS falls below its prior two-week level while RESIDENTIAL rises further, weather- or season-like confinement is dominating activity choices. That regime should reduce discretionary retail mobility within two weeks because people substitute home-based time for shopping and entertainment trips.
candidate_trigger: PARKS declines below its prior 2-week mean and RESIDENTIAL rises above it
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not weaken within two weeks after PARKS drops below its recent mean and RESIDENTIAL remains elevated.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL is rising and both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT are falling, the city is likely in a stay-at-home style regime that cuts outward trips. Retail-and-recreation mobility should keep declining over the next four weeks because household time is reallocating away from external discretionary activity.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decrease over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL stays above its recent level and both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT stay below.

mechanism_narrative: The synchronized deterioration in RETAIL_REC, TRANSIT, and WORKPLACES over the last two weeks suggests a momentum effect: once people reduce outside activity, the decline feeds on itself through habit and network effects. That self-reinforcing pattern should keep RETAIL_REC lower over the next week before any rebound can emerge.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both fall for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall further in the next week after two consecutive weekly declines in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES.
